messages:
alex: alert from observability-bot — hosted-api p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.1s in us-east-1 at ~21:02 UTC, affected traffic path = /v1/generate (spike ~21:02-21:04). seeing queue depth climb on inference nodes.
observability-bot: p99: 2.1s, p95: 480ms, tail at 99.9% 3.8s. spike correlates with sustained increase in small-concurrent requests (~1-3 tokens) from tenant: payroll-ops.
sara: thanks — any noisy-tenant tag? looks like tenant rate was within quota but bursty. can we see kernel selector logs?
jun: pulling kernel selection trace for ca.21:02. payload: model=gpt-small-2, seq=64 typical, but selector flipped between "vectorized-fp16" and "fallback-matmul" repeatedly. suspect churn in kernel scoring during the burst.
matt: also saw KV-cache hit-rate drop for those requests around the same window — prefetch sampler ramped up and caused excessive eviction churn. might explain increased latency when kernel flips + cache misses.
alex: can you paste the kernel selector snippet?
jun: paste below (trimmed):
```
[21:01:58] selector: model=gpt-small-2 seq=64 scores: vectorized-fp16=0.62, tiled-int8=0.58, fallback-matmul=0.61 -> choose vectorized-fp16
[21:02:01] selector: model=gpt-small-2 seq=64 scores: vectorized-fp16=0.59, tiled-int8=0.60, fallback-matmul=0.62 -> choose fallback-matmul
[21:02:03] selector: model=gpt-small-2 seq=64 scores: vectorized-fp16=0.63, tiled-int8=0.57, fallback-matmul=0.60 -> choose vectorized-fp16
[21:02:06] selector: churn detected, decisions toggling every 100-300ms for same host
```
jun: selector heuristic uses recent latency samples and kernel throughput model; with noisy microbursts it oscillates.
sara: that matches the KV-cache notes — if prefetch evicts prefixes, latency for same tenant jumps and selector reweights to fallback kernels (higher latency). vicious feedback.
matt: quick check: iostat/gpu util looked fine, but queue length on request-queue thread pools grew to 120 (target ~<50). backlog + kernel-swap = CPU/GPU context churn.
alex: proposed mitigation steps (short):
1) temporarily pin kernel for gpt-small-2 on the affected pool to vectorized-fp16 (force-stable)
2) throttle payroll-ops burstiness with a short token-bucket burst-reduction (soft limit)
3) roll back prefetch sampler change (ramp it down)
4) increase batcher max-delay from 5ms->10ms for the pool to smooth oscillation
which one do we want to try first?
sara: I'd prefer pinning kernel first (low blast radius) + ramp down prefetch. can we do a kernel-override on a canary host?
jun: i can push kernel-override to one host in the pool: command i will run: `rtctl kernel-override --pool=us-east-inf-4 --model=gpt-small-2 --kernel=vectorized-fp16 --duration=15m`
matt: also add a temporary routing policy to divert 5% of traffic away from that pool to dedicated-capacity to relieve saturation: `routingctl set-weight --pool=us-east-inf-4 --weight=0.95` (will send 5% elsewhere).
alex: go for canary kernel override + prefetch down-ramp. sara pls open a short incident note and flag CS (they'll want to know). i'll monitor p99.
sara: incident note created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-214 — adding payroll-ops PM and infra oncall.
jun: applied kernel-override to host inf-4a-canary. prefetch sampler throttle set to 0.2 (was 1.0). routing weight adjusted.
observability-bot: policy applied — canary: inf-4a -> vectorized-fp16. prefetch throttle=0.2. routing weight=0.95.
(monitoring) alex: 60s after override p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 420ms, p95 stable ~420-500ms. queue depth down to ~48. nice.
sara: good sign. need postmortem checklist items: - kernel selector smoothing (add hysteresis), - prefetch sampler guardrails (max evict rate), - batching max-delay dynamic tuning, - per-tenant burst detection to auto-throttle.
matt: agree. also add a short term perf regression test: run 10k synthetic small-concurrent requests against gpt-small-2 with both kernels and check selector stability. I'll add to perf CI.
alex: thanks team. next steps: jun to revert override after 15m if stable; sara to add incident tasks; matt to author perf test; eng-runtime to schedule a kernel-selector PR with hysteresis.
jun: noted — will revert override after 15m and capture full kernel decision trace for postmortem.
observability-bot: incident auto-close condition: p99 < 600ms for 10m. current state: p99=410ms, tail trending down.
alex: closing active triage. follow-up doc in #eng-runtime-docs with PR links. :thumbsup:
